title: Quasi-coherent etale cohomology is unchanged by coefficient universe lift
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] and F a quasi-coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Let F_et be its associated additive sheaf [def-sc-etale-qcoherent-module]. For every natural q there exists an additive equivalence H^q(X_et, ULift(F_et)) ≃+ H^q(X_et,F_et), where the left coefficients lie in AddCommGrpCat.{u+1} and the right coefficients lie in AddCommGrpCat.{u}. Both sides are the Ext-defined Sheaf.H groups. No curve, dimension, smoothness or vanishing hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 59.22.4, separated-case affine-cover Cech comparison; also Proposition 35.9.3 (03DW), part (2). Coefficient-universe comparison obtained by applying this same computation in each universe.

proof.text: In degree zero use H.equiv₀ on both sides, identify the large terminal section group definitionally with ULift of the small one, and compose with AddEquiv.ulift and the inverse small H.equiv₀. This case needs no affine cover.

For q=n+1, choose the finite subcover of the canonical affine open cover. Its opensRange family covers X, and IsAffineOpen.iInf proves each nonempty finite intersection affine by separatedness. Apply the positive-degree lifted finite-affine Cech comparison to this concrete cover.

Choose the canonical module Cech comparison c supplied by cechComparisonMapNaturality. Its affine-intersection theorem makes c an isomorphism to RingedSpace.moduleCohomology. With K the module Cech complex and T forget-scalars followed by ULift, ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso yields H(TK) isomorphic to T(H(K)); follow it by T.mapIso(asIso c), then unlift.

Use the existing etale-Zariski quasi-coherent comparison to identify module cohomology with the small etale cohomology. The comparison uses a standard large Ext model; identify it with the small Ext model through their homAddEquiv maps into one common derived category. Compose this with the lifted Cech and homology equivalences.

proof_origin.place: Separated affine-cover Cech argument, composed with the existing 03DW (2) and canonical module Cech comparisons. Degree zero is sectionwise; positive degrees use exactness of forget-scalars and ULift via ShortComplex.mapHomologyIso.
